simple.meaning: כָּשַׁל (kâshal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter , stumble , faint or fall.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 65 times across Leviticus, 1 Samuel, 2 Chronicles, Nehemiah, Job, and 11 more, beginning at Leviticus 26:37. Its contexts include family, sacrifice, kingship, city, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּשַׁל (H3782).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: כָּשַׁל (kâshal) / H3782 is traced through Leviticus 26:37, 1 Samuel 2:4, 2 Chronicles 25:8, 2 Chronicles 28:15 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter , stumble , faint or fall

occurrences.englishText: They will stumble over one another, as it were before the sword, when no one pursues. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.
“The bows of the mighty men are broken.
But if you will go, take action, and be strong for the battle. God will overthrow you before the enemy; for God has power to help, and to overthrow.”
But if you will go, take action, and be strong for the battle. God will overthrow you before the enemy; for God has power to help, and to overthrow.”

The men who have been mentioned by name rose up and took the captives, and with the plunder clothed all who were naked among them, dressed them, gave them sandals, and gave them something to eat and to drink, anointed them, carried all the feeble of them on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers. Then they returned to Samaria.

For he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, which struck him. He said, “Because the gods of the kings of Syria helped them, so I will sacrifice to them, that they may help me.” But they were the ruin of him, and of all Israel.
“Hear, our God; for we are despised. Turn back their reproach on their own head. Give them up for a plunder in a land of captivity.
Your words have supported him who was falling,
For you have maintained my just cause.
When evildoers came at me to eat up my flesh,
Because of all my adversaries I have become utterly contemptible to my neighbors,
All mankind shall be afraid.
He brought them out with silver and gold.
Therefore he brought down their heart with labor.
My knees are weak through fasting.
When you go, your steps will not be hampered.
For they don’t sleep unless they do evil.
For they don’t sleep unless they do evil.
The way of the wicked is like darkness.
for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again;
Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls.
For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen;
No one shall be weary nor stumble among them;
Many will stumble over it, fall, be broken, be snared, and be captured.”

Therefore Yahweh’s word will be to them precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little; that they may go, fall backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.
Now the Egyptians are men, and not God;
Strengthen the weak hands,
Even the youths faint and get weary,
Even the youths faint and get weary,
We grope for the wall like the blind.
Justice is turned away backward,
Who led them through the depths,
Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination?
Therefore Yahweh says, “Behold, I will lay stumbling blocks before this people. The fathers and the sons together will stumble against them. The neighbor and his friend will perish.”
Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination?
For my people have forgotten me.
Yet, Yahweh, you know all their counsel against me to kill me.
But Yahweh is with me as an awesome mighty one.
They will come with weeping.
“Don’t let the swift flee away,
The nations have heard of your shame,
He made many to stumble.
The proud one will stumble and fall,
“The yoke of my transgressions is bound by his hand.
The young men carry millstones.

“You, son of man, tell the children of your people, ‘The righteousness of the righteous will not deliver him in the day of his disobedience. And as for the wickedness of the wicked, he will not fall by it in the day that he turns from his wickedness; neither will he who is righteous be able to live by it in the day that he sins.
therefore you shall devour men no more, and not bereave your nation any more,” says the Lord Yahweh.
“I won’t let you hear the shame of the nations any more. You won’t bear the reproach of the peoples any more, and you won’t cause your nation to stumble any more,” says the Lord Yahweh.’ ”
“In those times many will stand up against the king of the south. Also the children of the violent among your people will lift themselves up to establish the vision; but they will fall.
Then he will turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land; but he will stumble and fall, and won’t be found.
“Those who are wise among the people will instruct many; yet they will fall by the sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, many days.
Now when they fall, they will be helped with a little help; but many will join themselves to them with flatteries.
Some of those who are wise will fall, to refine them, and to purify, and to make them white, even to the time of the end; because it is yet for the time appointed.
He will enter also into the glorious land, and many countries will be overthrown; but these will be delivered out of his hand: Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.
You will stumble in the day,
You will stumble in the day,
The pride of Israel testifies to his face.
The pride of Israel testifies to his face.
Take words with you, and return to Yahweh.
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
the horseman mounting, and the flashing sword, the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies. They stumble on their bodies,

In that day Yahweh will defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem. He who is feeble among them at that day will be like David, and David’s house will be like God, like Yahweh’s angel before them.
But you have turned away from the path. You have caused many to stumble in the law. You have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says Yahweh of Armies.
